title: Bi-Continuous W-Rich Refractory High Entropy Alloy-Cu Composite: Toward Material Innovation of Nuclear Reactor Coolant System.

recollection.starting_material: Likely a mixture of W-rich refractory high entropy alloy and copper
recollection.intervention: Probably fabrication of a bi-continuous composite structure, possibly via powder metallurgy or casting
recollection.structure: A bi-continuous composite with interpenetrating networks of W-rich HEA and Cu
recollection.mechanism: The bi-continuous structure would allow for combining high strength and thermal conductivity, with the HEA providing mechanical robustness and Cu providing thermal transport
recollection.results: Main quantitative results likely include improved thermal conductivity compared to pure HEA, enhanced mechanical properties compared to pure Cu, and possibly radiation resistance relevant for nuclear reactor coolant systems

score.note: The recollection does not identify liquid-metal dealloying in molten Cu at 1200 °C for 96 h and instead speculates about powder metallurgy or casting. It gives only the title-level bicontinuous RHEA–Cu structure and a generic strength/thermal-transport rationale, omitting the aligned ligaments/channels, W-rich interlayer, selective Ti–Cu exchange mechanism, irradiation mechanism, and all quantitative results.
